did_you_know.text: Did you know? At the beginning of the chapter, the people read from the Book of Moses and find the prohibition against Ammonites and Moabites entering the assembly of the Lord. This highlights the connection between reading the Torah and reforming public life.
Did you know? After hearing the Torah, the people separated from Israel everyone of Ammonite and Moabite descent, in accordance with the command mentioned in the reading.
Did you know? Eliashib the priest, who was closely associated with Tobiah, gave him a large chamber in the temple courts—an improper use of a space intended for the needs of the temple.
Did you know? When Nehemiah returned to Jerusalem and saw the chamber given to Tobiah, he threw all his belongings out and restored the room for use by the house of God.

Did you know? Nehemiah discovered that the Levites had not received their portions, so they were forced to leave their service and return to their fields. The chapter connects material support with the continuation of temple worship.
Did you know? Nehemiah saw people in Judah treading winepresses, transporting produce, and bringing it into Jerusalem on the Sabbath, and he warned them against profaning the Sabbath.
Did you know? To prevent commerce on the Sabbath, Nehemiah ordered the gates of Jerusalem to be closed before the Sabbath and stationed guards so that no loads would enter on the holy day.

Did you know? The Levites were instructed to purify themselves and guard the gates in order to keep the Sabbath day holy. In this way, the chapter brings together purification, public responsibility, and the observance of sacred time.

Did you know? Intermarriage resulted in some of the children in these families speaking Ashdodite and not knowing the language of Judah; the chapter presents this as a social and linguistic consequence of assimilation.
Did you know? One member of the high priest’s family—the son of Joiada, son of Eliashib—was the son-in-law of Sanballat the Horonite, and Nehemiah drove him away because of this connection.
